papers.title: UnAct: Gradient-Free Unlearning via Targeted Activation Intervention
papers.problem: A model must forget one class, but current methods break the model when only a few images are available.
papers.fix: UnAct forgets a class using only forward passes, stays within 2.5 points of retraining, and runs 19x faster than SSD.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can honor a deletion request with a few images, so try this before paying for full retraining.
papers.limitation: Tests used small image models on CIFAR data, and the transfer to a larger model is only preliminary.

papers.title: LoGRA: Scaling LLM Reinforcement Learning with Low-Rank Gradient Sketches
papers.problem: Reinforcement learning for language models needs so much memory that many teams cannot run it.
papers.fix: LoGRA cuts training memory by up to 45.7% without losing performance, and trains a 27B model on one node.
papers.practicalUseCase: Big-model reinforcement learning now fits on one machine, so try memory-saving gradient compression before renting a larger cluster.
papers.limitation: The excerpt reports results on reasoning tasks only, so other tasks may behave differently.

papers.title: Capability-Driven Self-Evolution of Agent Memory
papers.problem: Memory programs for AI agents improve by overall score, which hides gains in single skills and losses elsewhere.
papers.fix: PrisMem improves single skills separately, then merges them, and beats the best baselines by 10.54 and 7.83 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: Track each agent memory skill on its own, because one overall score can hide real gains and real regressions.
papers.limitation: The gains come from two long-history benchmarks, so real products may see smaller gains.

papers.title: SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting
papers.problem: Forecasts that use only past numbers miss shocks from outside events, and news retrieval adds noise and missing signals.
papers.fix: SEER learns from its forecast errors to improve news search, and it beats leading forecasting models on six volatile benchmarks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Feed event news into forecasts and learn from errors, but keep strict time limits so future data never leaks in.
papers.limitation: Results come from six benchmarks, and the excerpt gives no gain size, so real-world gains remain unclear.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Few people know how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what decides the size of each issue.
papers.fix: In 11,944 sukuk, growth centers in Indonesia, Malaysia and Saudi Arabia, and equity contracts raise issue size.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers in other Muslim-majority countries should note that equity-based contracts, strong security and USD or Euro denomination help larger issues.
papers.limitation: The data ends in 2022 and shows links between features and size, not proof of cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks lack clear evidence on which national factors drive growth in a dual banking system.
papers.fix: In 218 banks across 12 countries, ICT adoption drives bank growth most, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital tools matter more than exports for bank growth, so invest in digital systems first and strengthen governance next.
papers.limitation: The study covers 12 countries and shows statistical links, so results may differ in other places.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan do not know whether AI and big data help them compete and grow sustainably.
papers.fix: AI, big data skills and data management link to competitiveness and sustainability, but staff digital skill links only to competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic banks should fund AI, big data and data management, and not expect staff digital skill alone to improve sustainability.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers at 15 Jordanian banks at one time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Financial inclusion stays low in many Muslim-majority countries, even though Islamic finance has expanded.
papers.fix: In OIC countries, income, tertiary education, institutions, internet access, population and age dependency all shape financial inclusion.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC governments should invest in digital infrastructure, youth and women empowerment, and income growth to widen financial inclusion.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries and reports statistical links, so single countries may differ.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but nobody knows if these committees change real environmental results.
papers.fix: Committees improve all four environmental measures at conventional banks, but only overall scores and resource reduction at Islamic banks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do not trust a sustainability committee alone at an Islamic bank, so check for real green products and innovation.
papers.limitation: The study shows statistical links in emerging markets, not proof that committees cause the results.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant testing and comparison, and nobody had pooled how often they feel like frauds.
papers.fix: A review of many studies finds impostor feelings are frequent among medical students, though results vary a lot between studies.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud while training, know that many peers do too, so talk about it early.
papers.limitation: Studies differ widely in method and region, so the pooled estimate needs careful reading.

papers.title: Positive mood enhances accessibility of unrelated concepts in the first language but not in the foreign language
papers.problem: Researchers did not know how mood changes word meaning access in a first language versus a foreign one.
papers.fix: Positive mood makes distant ideas easier to reach in the first language, but not in the foreign language.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do your creative thinking and brainstorming in your first language when in a good mood.
papers.limitation: This brain-signal study tests word processing only, so it may not predict real workplace results.
